question: Should status output show exact cumulative transcript-backed cost, and if so must the implementation use a bounded or maintained aggregate instead of full transcript scans on default status paths?
rationale: The user-facing request is useful and vision-aligned, but the open implementation has a status responsiveness tradeoff that automation should not decide as product policy.

options.title: Use bounded aggregate
options.body: Keep this issue open and require the linked implementation to show cumulative cost from a bounded, cached, persisted, or otherwise maintained aggregate before merge.

options.title: Accept exact scans
options.body: Allow exact transcript-backed cost even if default status may scan large transcripts, with clear maintainer acceptance of the responsiveness tradeoff.

options.title: Defer status display
options.body: Leave cumulative cost in `/usage cost` and Usage UI only until a broader session-aggregate design exists.

recommendation.title: Use bounded aggregate
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require the linked implementation to show cumulative cost from a bounded, cached, persisted, or otherwise maintained aggregate before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent status rendering history and current line ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the status UX and fast-path decision.
